No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

The lecture follows an archaeological site from the first survey to the museum shelf: how a site is located, how a trench is laid out and recorded, what happens to finds in the laboratory, and what becomes of a site once excavation ends.

Length, level and language are agreed with you. The lecture can be given online or at your venue, for a single class, a department or a whole organisation.

What it covers

  • How sites are found
  • How a trench is laid out, dug and recorded
  • What happens to finds in the laboratory
  • What becomes of a site after the dig

How the time is spent

  1. Questions to evidence 20 min

    Site selection, evidence and recording.

    You: build question

  2. Field workflow 35 min

    Survey, context sheets, finds, samples.

    You: mock context card

  3. Interpretation 20 min

    Reporting, ethics and uncertainty.

    You: one-page report

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Explain how archaeological sites are found and why a site is selected for study.
  • Describe how a trench is laid out, dug and recorded, including context sheets.
  • Trace what happens to finds in the laboratory and to a site after the dig.
